tagline: Every force goes somewhere. Every boundary is a choice.

books.title: The Ninth Standard
books.description: Kade Mercer: zero output score, last-ranked freshman, impossible boundary architecture. The academy that rejected him becomes the one thing he has to save.

books.title: The Quiet Ward
books.description: Dr. Sable Hren. Room Four. A patient whose field instruments return null — not low, not zero. Null. Thirty-three days to learn what the instruments cannot say.

books.title: Contact Zero
books.description: Station engineer Aaron Mercer discovers an anomalous array that should not exist and cannot be explained. The signal it carries is not a malfunction. It is addressed.

chapters.title: The Kid in Room Four
chapters.summary: Northline Alternative. Kade is introduced through a school day that shows intelligence, boredom, defensive humor and the social ecology of kids the mainstream system has rejected. National Aptitude Ascension Examination ends with score 000 and a system-wide failure.

chapters.title: Zero Protocol
chapters.summary: Government response arrives before midnight. Kade expects discipline and instead meets restricted officials. His mother forces the emotional issue: he has demanded a real chance for years; now he is afraid to take one.

chapters.title: Asterion
chapters.summary: Arrival by sea/air. Sensory immersion in campus, rankings, spectacle and class disparity. Kade's belongings feel painfully small next to elite peers.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Four Hundred Eighty-Two
chapters.summary: Baseline testing. Nearly no measurable output. Official last place. Rumors of Zero Boy become humiliation rather than mystique.

chapters.title: House Meridian
chapters.summary: Dorm ensemble chapter. Eli, Mara, Sera, Taren. Dining hall, house traditions, first glimpse of Julian and a Standard Six duel. Kade begins wanting what he insists he does not need.

chapters.title: Forty-Seven Seconds
chapters.summary: First combat assessment. Kade loses but performs impossible-looking momentum routing in the final seconds. Faculty quietly flag the footage.

chapters.title: The Suppression Order
chapters.summary: Sen orders conservative training limits. Kade hears a distorted version. Campus interprets it as institutional suppression. End Act I: Kade decides if they want him last, he will climb anyway.

chapters.title: The Ladder
chapters.summary: Challenge rules and early climb. Multiple short fights show learning, not effortless dominance. Eli starts keeping a private tactical model.

chapters.title: Meridian Night
chapters.summary: Social breathing room. Party, academy rituals, status anxiety, first real Kade/Mara conversation. Julian unexpectedly prevents Kade's public embarrassment.

chapters.title: Vector Class
chapters.summary: Formal physics instruction exposes gaps in Kade's education. He is brilliant conceptually but weak in notation. Mara reluctantly tutors him after he helps her see a practical flaw.

chapters.title: The Broken Floor
chapters.summary: Ranked bout against #2,301. Kade redefines opponent-floor-arena boundary and dumps force into structure. Floor fractures. Match frozen.

chapters.title: Boundary Conditions
chapters.summary: Sen gives Kade a partial explanation. First use of term boundary architecture. She lies when he asks if anyone has done it before.

chapters.title: Cross Examination
chapters.summary: Julian privately spars with Kade and repeatedly destroys him. Rival becomes mentor-peer. Kade learns rare does not mean skilled.

chapters.title: House Trial: Qualifiers
chapters.summary: Team strategy, politics and ensemble competence. Meridian overperforms. Kade's role works because he empowers others.

chapters.title: House Trial: Final
chapters.summary: Large team set piece. Kade and Mara coordinate instinctively. Meridian wins. Kade jumps to #1,904. Midpoint: he becomes famous.

chapters.title: Famous for Tuesday
chapters.summary: Interviews, sponsorships, memes, social consequences. Humor and discomfort. Kade discovers success can alienate as effectively as failure.

chapters.title: Home
chapters.summary: Visit Northline. Mixed reactions from teachers/students. Former teacher claims credit; another apologizes. Kade invites Northline students to Asterion. Emotional midpoint.

chapters.title: The Vey Problem
chapters.summary: Mara-focused material. Her father asks specific questions about Kade he should not know to ask. She begins investigating independently.

chapters.title: Aaron Mercer
chapters.summary: Kade finds archived record of a Zero candidate from 31 years earlier: his father. Industrial-accident story begins collapsing.

chapters.title: Run
chapters.summary: Kade attempts to leave. Sera calls out preemptive abandonment. He stays, but not because he trusts Asterion—because he chooses his people.

chapters.title: Midyear: Open Rounds
chapters.summary: Tournament begins. Multiple bouts show earned progression and persistent weaknesses.

chapters.title: Midyear: Mercer v. Vey
chapters.summary: Kade faces Mara. She defeats him by planning beyond his improvisational horizon. Their mutual respect deepens; attraction becomes undeniable to everyone but them.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Name
chapters.summary: Kade/Eli investigation reveals only eleven Standard Eights publicly, but twelve historical identifiers. Aaron is the missing twelfth.

chapters.title: The Quiet War
chapters.summary: Sen gives partial truth: Contact Zero, nonhuman technology, academies as more than sport. Kade realizes the institution can be both home and machine.

chapters.title: Taren Holt
chapters.summary: Taren helps break into restricted archive, then traps Kade. Reveal: his original friendship was an assignment. Crucially, Taren's later friendship became real.

chapters.title: Lab Six
chapters.summary: Attack/explosion. Eli listed dead. Kade believes his investigation killed his first real friend.

chapters.title: The Empty Bed
chapters.summary: Grief chapter. Dorm, funeral preparations, fractured friendships. Avoid action. Kade nearly regresses completely.

chapters.title: Memorial
chapters.summary: Kade speaks publicly and admits Eli mattered. End beat: dead-channel message—'DUDE. DO NOT FREAK OUT.'

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Eli survived with Sen's help after detecting surveillance. Suppression order reframed as protection. The conspiracy has people inside Asterion.

chapters.title: Siege of Asterion
chapters.summary: Faction moves openly. Students and faculty fight across familiar campus spaces. Tournament techniques meet real violence; consequences are frightening.

chapters.title: Aaron
chapters.summary: Sealed chamber opened. Aaron Mercer alive, sustaining containment around the Refuge Node. Father-son reunion is angry, incomplete and emotionally messy.

chapters.title: Consensus
chapters.summary: Climax. Kade understands Ninth Standard as multi-person boundary control. He cannot command it; he must invite it. Mara, Julian, Sera, Taren, Eli and Meridian join. Stable Consensus prevents catastrophe.

chapters.title: First Day
chapters.summary: Aftermath, rank reset, consequences, partial accountability. Kade/Mara acknowledge attraction without a neat ending. Long-range signal receives coordinates and countdown. Kade's new rank is #37; Standard reads NINE.
